subtitle: Code current through legislation of 06-17-2026 (eCode360 download) · Prepared Nov 16, 2026 · @SEAN

howToUse.value: Every section number here was checked against the Township of Wayne General Code (eCode360 download dated 11-16-2026, which covers legislation through 06-17-2026). Ordinances amended after that date are not reflected. Before an unusual or contested charge, confirm the section on eCode360 or with the municipal prosecutor.

howToUse.label: Citation format
howToUse.value: Write it on the complaint-summons as Wayne Code § 121-9F: chapter, section, and subsection letter or number.

howToUse.label: Penalty
howToUse.value: Many sections refer to the general penalty in § 1-15 (see General Penalty Provision near the end). Where a chapter sets its own fine, that fine is listed.

howToUse.label: Who enforces
howToUse.value: Each entry shows the enforcing authority the code names. If the code names someone else (for example, the Construction Official or Health Officer), patrol should document the condition and refer it rather than sign the complaint, unless the code also names police.

howToUse.label: Noise authority
howToUse.value: § 123-5 designates the Chief of Police or his/her designee as Noise Control Investigators (NCIs). Patrol can enforce noise rules based on plainly audible, time of day, or distance, with no sound meter. Rules that need a meter reading (decibel tables) belong to a certified Noise Control Officer.

howToUse.label: "State overlap — verify"
howToUse.value: marks a related NJ statute. It is not part of the Wayne code. Confirm the state charge separately before using it.

intro.value: Patrol enforces noise as Noise Control Investigators under § 123-5, using plainly audible, time of day and distance. Chapter 121 citations go through the NOV/NOPA process in § 121-11. § 123-4 and § 123-4.1 go to court under § 1-15.

intro.label: § 121-11 process (applies to every Chapter 121 entry)
intro.value: A minor violation gets a Notice of Violation (NOV) with a grace period of up to 90 days. A non-minor violation gets a Notice of Penalty Assessment (NOPA) if it is not corrected immediately. If it is corrected, an NOV is still issued. A repeat within 12 months gets a NOPA either way. Civil penalty: up to $2,000 per offense, with each day a separate offense (§ 121-11B). The recipient may contest a NOPA in municipal court (§ 121-11G).
Chapter 200 violations carry a fine of up to $75, up to 15 days, or both (§ 200-3), unless a section below says otherwise. Street-by-street restrictions are in the schedules at §§ 200-29 to 200-48.1.

Every Chapter 60 violation carries the same fine: $100 for a first offense, $500 for a second and $1,000 for a third (§ 60-11A). The Chief may also suspend a permit pending a revocation hearing (§ 60-8C).

Most Chapter 112 violations are punished as unlawful solid waste disposal: a minimum fine of $2,500 and a maximum of $10,000, with each day a separate violation, plus the Township's cleanup cost (§ 112-16C; § 1-15.1B and § 1-15.2B). Chapter 112 does not name a police enforcer except where noted, so confirm department practice on who signs.

Animal control officers are the primary enforcers, but § 68-15 states that nothing limits the Chief's or police officers' authority to enforce Chapter 68. Unless noted, the penalty is § 1-15 (§ 68-6.1B; § 68-67).

Park rules in § 129-20 are enforced by Parks and Recreation staff and by the Wayne Police Department (§ 129-20E(4)). Staff may eject violators and seize items used in a violation (§ 129-20E(2)–(3)). The penalty is § 1-15 (§ 129-27B).

entries.title: Disturbing the peace — Wayne Code § 123-4
entries.name: Disturbing the peace

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Unnecessary noise from a voice or a sound device that is plainly audible and excessive across a real property line and unreasonably disturbs a resident. Applies on premises the person controls or on a public street.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Plainly audible across the property line; excessive; unreasonably disturbs a resident. The code defines "unusual time" to include "10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. on weekdays" and 11 p.m.–9 a.m. on weekends.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Chief of Police or designee (§ 123-5).

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: Not required by the code.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Note where you stood, the time, and what you heard from the complainant's side of the line.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 2C:33-2 (disorderly conduct).

entries.title: Portable music in public — Wayne Code § 121-9F
entries.name: Portable music in public

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Portable, non-vehicle music or sound devices on a public space or right-of-way that are plainly audible beyond a set distance.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Plainly audible at 50 ft from the operator (8 a.m.–10 p.m.) or 25 ft (10 p.m.–8 a.m.).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: NCO/NCI; police as NCIs (§ 123-5).

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: NOV if minor; NOPA if non-minor and not corrected (§ 121-11D–E).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Pace off or estimate the distance and record it.

entries.title: Vehicle stereos — Wayne Code § 121-10C and § 121-10D
entries.name: Vehicle stereos

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Vehicle music equipment that is plainly audible beyond a set distance.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: § 121-10C: plainly audible at 25 ft, 10 p.m.–8 a.m. § 121-10D: plainly audible at 50 ft, 8 a.m.–10 p.m. The code says the rhythmic bass alone is enough for "plainly audible" (§ 121-2).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: No grace period. § 121-10 violations are deemed purposeful and therefore non-minor.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: You don't need to identify the song or the artist.

entries.title: Modified exhaust and motorcycle mufflers — Wayne Code § 121-10A and § 121-10B
entries.name: Modified exhaust and motorcycle mufflers

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (A) Removing or disabling a vehicle's factory noise-control equipment, or driving a vehicle modified that way. (B) Running a motorcycle without a muffler labeled under federal rule 40 CFR Part 205.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: The vehicle is on a public space or right-of-way, moving or stationary. Maintenance or repair is exempt.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 121-11 (up to $2,000). Non-minor by definition.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: No.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 39:3-70 (mufflers).

entries.title: Residential power tools and yard equipment — Wayne Code § 121-9A
entries.name: Residential power tools and yard equipment

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A homeowner or tenant running power tools, home maintenance or yard equipment between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m., unless the meter limits are met. Motorized equipment must have a muffler.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Time; the user is the owner or tenant; not emergency work.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: NOV if minor.

entries.title: Commercial landscaping — Wayne Code § 121-9B
entries.name: Commercial landscaping

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Commercial operators or public employees using power tools or landscaping equipment 6 p.m.–8 a.m. on weekdays, or 6 p.m.–9 a.m. on weekends and federal holidays.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Time; nonresidential operator; not emergency work.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: NOV if minor.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: "Weekday" runs from Monday 7 a.m. to Friday 6 p.m. (§ 121-2).

entries.title: Construction and demolition hours — Wayne Code § 121-9C
entries.name: Construction and demolition hours

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Construction or demolition 6 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekdays, or 6 p.m.–9 a.m. on weekends and federal holidays.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Time; construction or demolition activity; not emergency work.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: NOV if minor.

entries.title: Burglar alarms (building or vehicle) — Wayne Code § 121-9E
entries.name: Burglar alarms (building or vehicle)

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: An alarm that does not shut off within 5 minutes (continuous sound) or 15 minutes (intermittent).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 121-11. A separate charge under § 36-4B covers outdoor building alarms (see Alarms).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs.

entries.title: Animal noise — Wayne Code § 121-9G (also § 68-14)
entries.name: Animal noise

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: An owner or tenant letting an animal make sound across a property line that unreasonably disturbs a resident, or refusing to stop it when an NCO/NCI orders.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Prima facie: vocalizing 5 minutes without interruption (average 4 or more per minute), or 20 minutes intermittently (average 2 or more per minute). § 68-14 uses the same thresholds for dogs.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police as NCIs; animal control officers and police for Chapter 68 (§ 68-15).

fields.label: Defense
fields.value: It is an affirmative defense that the animal was intentionally provoked.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Time the barking yourself and log the count.

entries.title: Engine compression (jake) brakes — Wayne Code § 123-4.1
entries.name: Engine compression (jake) brakes

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Using an engine compression brake that makes excessive, loud noise on these roads: Alps Rd (Maple Ave to Rt 23), Central Ave, Dorsa Ave, French Hill Rd (Alps Rd to Parish Dr), Haul Rd, Maple Ave, Oldham Rd, Parish Dr, Preakness Ave, Ratzer Rd, Ryerson Ave and Whitmore Ave.

fields.label: Exempt
fields.value: Public safety vehicles, and emergencies where the driver reasonably believes the brake is needed to protect people or property.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Chief of Police or designee (§ 123-5).

fields.label: Meter-only rules (refer to a certified NCO)
fields.value: § 121-7 sets decibel limits by property type and time, for example 65 dBA by day and 50 dBA at night at a residential line. § 121-8 limits indoor dB(C) increases from sound devices. Both require a sound level meter.

entries.title: Overnight parking (2 a.m.–6 a.m.) — Wayne Code § 200-5B
entries.name: Overnight parking (2 a.m.–6 a.m.)

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Parking on any street between 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m.

fields.label: Exempt streets (§ 200-29C)
fields.value: Atherton Ct (from Valley Rd to the Building 8 and 11 entrances), Byrne Ct (west side), Knox Terrace (north side), Lancaster Ct, Manchester Ct, Old Newark Pompton Tpk, Royal Ct, Salisbury Rd and Traphagen Rd.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: No.

entries.title: Posted restrictions (no parking, time limits, no stopping) — Wayne Code §§ 200-5A, 200-6, 200-7, 200-8
entries.name: Posted restrictions (no parking, time limits, no stopping)

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Parking against a scheduled restriction: no parking at any time (§ 200-5A, Schedule I), during set hours (§ 200-6, Schedule II), stopping or standing (§ 200-7, Schedule III), or past a time limit (§ 200-8, Schedule IV).

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: The street and side are in the schedule; the time window applies.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Check that the street is listed in the schedule before writing. Cite the operative section (for example, § 200-6) and note the schedule.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 39:4-138 (statewide no-parking zones such as crosswalks, driveways and intersections).

entries.title: Snow on the roadway — Wayne Code § 200-22
entries.name: Snow on the roadway

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Parking on any street or highway while snow covers the streets, until plowing is done enough that parking won't block traffic.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 200-3. The vehicle may be towed at the owner's cost (§ 200-24).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police; "any peace officer" may have the vehicle removed (§ 200-24).

fields.label: Caution
fields.value: § 200-25 makes this article effective only where signs are posted as required by law. Confirm signage before charging.

entries.title: Emergency no-parking — Wayne Code § 200-23
entries.name: Emergency no-parking

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Parking where temporary emergency no-parking signs are posted after an emergency is declared.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: The Chief, or in his absence the ranking officer, declared the emergency (weather, crashes, fires, celebrations). Owners of vehicles parked before the signs went up must be notified (§ 200-23B).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 200-3; towing under § 200-24.

entries.title: Hydrants and fire department connections — Wayne Code § 205-38B
entries.name: Hydrants and fire department connections

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Standing or parking within 10 ft of a fire hydrant or fire department connection. Applies on public, semipublic or private property and roadways.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Fine up to $50, up to 15 days, or both. The vehicle is towed at the owner's expense.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: This section covers private lots, too.

entries.title: Handicapped parking (off-street public and semipublic lots) — Wayne Code § 200-10.2
entries.name: Handicapped parking (off-street public and semipublic lots)

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Standing or parking in a posted disabled space without the MVC placard, plate or insignia. The placard goes in the lower right corner of the windshield (§ 200-10.3). Damaging a disabled-parking sign is a separate violation (§ 200-10.4).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $250 first offense; at least $250 and up to 90 days community service after that (§ 200-10.5).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police.

entries.title: Private lots under Title 39 (malls, shopping centers, schools, condos) — Wayne Code § 200-10
entries.name: Private lots under Title 39 (malls, shopping centers, schools, condos)

fields.label: What it does
fields.value: Applies Title 39 and the listed traffic controls on private properties whose owners asked for it. The properties are listed in Schedules VI, VIA, VIB, VIC and VII (§§ 200-34 to 200-35.70), including Willowbrook Mall, Wayne Towne Centre and the high schools.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Title 39 enforcement on a private lot is valid only if the property is listed. Check the schedule first.

entries.title: Truck exclusions (over 4 tons) — Wayne Code § 200-11
entries.name: Truck exclusions (over 4 tons)

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Trucks over 4 tons gross weight on the streets in Schedule VIII (§ 200-36), except for pickup and delivery on those streets.

entries.title: Boats, campers and trailers in residential driveways — Wayne Code § 134-67.1A
entries.name: Boats, campers and trailers in residential driveways

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (1) Storing boats, commercial or recreational trailers, mobile homes or RVs in a front-yard driveway. They may go in a side or rear yard at least 5 ft from the side line and 10 ft from the rear line. (2) Parking vehicles anywhere other than a paved driveway; no parking on grass.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Up to $1,250 or 90 days (§ 134-122). Each day after 10 days' written notice is a separate offense.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Zoning Officer / Construction Official. Refer it.

entries.title: Commercial vehicles in residential zones — Wayne Code § 134-67.1B
entries.name: Commercial vehicles in residential zones

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: No more than one commercial vehicle, school bus or limousine parked overnight. It must weigh no more than 15,000 lbs GVWR, be registered to the occupant or the occupant's employer, and sit on a paved surface. It may be no more than 84 in. wide or high and no more than 240 in. long.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Zoning Officer. Refer it.

entries.title: Abandoned and junk vehicles — Wayne Code § 198-3 and § 198-4
entries.name: Abandoned and junk vehicles

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (§ 198-3) Leaving an abandoned vehicle outdoors on public or private land or a street. "Abandoned" means no current registration, or so disabled that it obstructs traffic and the owner won't move it. (§ 198-4) Keeping a junk automobile on any property.

fields.label: Exempt
fields.value: Vehicles in a garage or building, lawful junkyards, vehicles held at a lawful repair or sales business, and unregistered vehicles used only on private property.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police impound abandoned or stolen vehicles; fees are under Chapter 191 (§ 198-3.1). For junk autos, the violation begins after 10 days' notice from the Property Maintenance Official.

entries.title: Roll-off dumpsters — Wayne Code § 83-10 and § 83-11
entries.name: Roll-off dumpsters

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (§ 83-10) A roll-off dumpster on a municipal road or property without a Construction Official permit, which is valid for no more than 30 days. In the road it needs 18 in. x 18 in. reflective diamond panels at both ends, mounted at least 3 ft high, and reflective cones around it. (§ 83-11) A dumpster on private property without a permit; more than 48 hours without an active construction permit; or within 10 ft of a property line unless fully in a paved driveway.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 83-12: $500–$10,000, with each day a separate violation (Article I). § 83-11E points to § 1-15.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Construction Official; the Chief of Police or designee reviews street placements (§ 83-10D).

entries.title: Road work zones — Wayne Code §§ 200-52 to 200-60
entries.name: Road work zones

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: Work in the roadway must follow the MUTCD (§ 200-52B). Contractors must hold a preconstruction meeting with the Traffic Bureau (§ 200-53). No work on Traffic Bureau-listed heavily traveled roads before 9 a.m. or after 4 p.m. (§ 200-56). Road closings and detours need Traffic Bureau approval (§ 200-57). Intersections with signals need a police officer, not a civilian flagger (§ 200-58C).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: The Wayne PD Traffic Bureau can stop work (§ 200-59).

entries.title: Permit required — Wayne Code § 60-2
entries.name: Permit required

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Commercial canvassing, soliciting in a public place, going house to house, selling by sample, or taking orders for goods or services without a written permit from the Chief of Police.

fields.label: Exempt from the permit only (§ 60-1B)
fields.value: Delivery of ordered goods; holders of a state or county license who carry employer ID; resident honorably discharged veterans or exempt firefighters with a state peddler's license (N.J.S.A. 45:24-9 and 45:24-10); political campaigning; noncommercial canvassing.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police (Records and Investigation Bureau issues permits).

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: No.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Permits expire December 31 (§ 60-3). The permit carries the holder's photo and must be worn where the public can see it (§ 60-5B).

entries.title: Conduct rules (apply to everyone, permitted or exempt) — Wayne Code § 60-7
entries.name: Conduct rules (apply to everyone, permitted or exempt)

fields.label: § 60-7A
fields.value: Circulars and samples must be handed to an occupant or left in a secure place.

fields.label: § 60-7B
fields.value: No entering a home without the occupant's express invitation.

fields.label: § 60-7C
fields.value: No claiming exclusive rights to a street location or blocking the public in congested areas.

fields.label: § 60-7D
fields.value: No soliciting where a sign prohibits it.

fields.label: § 60-7E
fields.value: No littering streets or property with merchandise or printed material.

fields.label: § 60-7F
fields.value: No soliciting on a public roadway or right-of-way, or from a vehicle in the roadway.

fields.label: § 60-7G
fields.value: No soliciting between 7:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m.

fields.label: § 60-7H
fields.value: Licensees must carry the license, show it to any resident on request, and display ID while soliciting.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: Applying the hours limit (§ 60-7G) to noncommercial, political or religious canvassers raises First Amendment issues. Check with the prosecutor before charging them.

entries.title: Nonsolicitation list — Wayne Code § 60-10
entries.name: Nonsolicitation list

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A permit holder canvassing, soliciting or peddling at any address on the Township Clerk's nonsolicitation list (§ 60-10B).

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: The address was on the list given to the permittee. The Clerk updates it quarterly on Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1 and Oct 1.

fields.label: Public education
fields.value: Residents sign up on a form at the Township Clerk's office (§ 60-10A).

entries.title: Handbills and flyers
entries.name: Handbills and flyers

fields.value: See Littering below: flyers on driveways (§ 112-4B–E) and on vehicles (§ 112-11).

entries.title: Illegal dumping — Wayne Code § 112-14
entries.name: Illegal dumping

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (A) Dumping solid waste along any street or road, on or off the right-of-way, or in any body of water. (B) Dumping on any public or private property without the owner's written consent, and then only in a proper container. Covers household, commercial and industrial waste; appliances, furniture, vehicles, parts and tires; construction debris; and leaves, brush and tree waste.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $2,500–$10,000 per day, plus cleanup cost (§ 112-16C).

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: No.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Photograph the debris and look for addressed mail or receipts in it. Note any vehicle or plate seen.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 13:1E-9.3 (illegal dumping) and N.J.S.A. 2C:17-2.

entries.name: Littering from a vehicle

fields.value: A driver or passenger throwing or depositing litter on a street, other public place or private property.

fields.label: State overlap — verify

entries.title: Litter on public, vacant or private property — Wayne Code §§ 112-2, 112-12, 112-4A
entries.name: Litter on public, vacant or private property

fields.value: No placing anything on a street, public place, public parking lot or public building that blocks it or makes it unsightly. Litter in public cans must be secured against wind.

fields.label: § 112-4A
fields.value: No leaving litter or bulk items (appliances, furniture, mattresses, tires) outside on private property, except in an enclosed structure or on bulk collection days.

fields.value: The Health Officer or designee abates and liens after 5 days' notice (§ 112-16A).

entries.title: Unsolicited flyers on property — Wayne Code § 112-4B to § 112-4E
entries.name: Unsolicited flyers on property

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Unsolicited flyers or shoppers must go in a receptacle meant for them. If there is none, they go on the ground under the mailbox or within 3 ft of it. Delivery must stop once the owner has sent a certified-mail stop request.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: The code is inconsistent. § 112-4F says up to $100 per delivery, while § 112-16C says up to $500 per improper distribution. Confirm with the prosecutor.

entries.title: Handbills on vehicles — Wayne Code § 112-11
entries.name: Handbills on vehicles

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Placing any commercial or noncommercial handbill on a vehicle. It is allowed to hand a free noncommercial handbill to a willing occupant in a public place.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Up to $500 (§ 112-16C, printed matter).

entries.title: Loads, mud and spilled debris — Wayne Code § 112-9
entries.name: Loads, mud and spilled debris

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (A) Hauling stone, dirt, sand, gravel, fill, clippings or waste without a tarp. The operator or owner is liable for any spill even if the load was covered. (B) Tracking mud or debris onto a street. (C) Failing to clean up immediately after glass or debris falls from a vehicle.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Director of Public Works or designee (§ 112-9D).

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 39:4-77 (spilling loads).

entries.title: Sidewalks, bins and construction sites — Wayne Code §§ 112-3, 112-7, 112-8, 112-15
entries.name: Sidewalks, bins and construction sites

fields.value: No sweeping litter into a gutter, street or catch basin. Owners and occupants must keep sidewalks and lots in front of their property free of litter.
Owners and occupants must keep the abutting sidewalk and curb free of obstructions and nuisances.
No open or overflowing waste bins on the property.
Construction sites must have adequate containers and must not let litter build up.

entries.title: Garbage set-out times — Wayne Code § 83-5D
entries.name: Garbage set-out times

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Garbage goes to the curb no earlier than the day before collection and no later than 6:00 a.m. on collection day. Cans must be removed the day of collection and stored out of sight. Cans are limited to 35 gallons and 50 lbs with tight lids (§ 83-5A).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: A written warning for the first violation, then § 1-15. (§ 83-12 separately lists $500–$10,000 for Article I; confirm which the prosecutor uses.)

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: Yes. A written warning is required.

entries.title: Recycling and yard waste set-out — Wayne Code § 141-4C and § 141-4D
entries.name: Recycling and yard waste set-out

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Recycling and yard waste go to the curb no earlier than the day before collection and by 6:00 a.m. on collection day. Containers must be removed the day of collection. Yard waste must be in paper bags or containers of 32–35 gallons. No plastic bags, and no loose yard waste in or on the curb or street.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 141-4D: written warning, then § 1-15. § 141-10A: $100–$500, with one written warning to residents first.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Director of Public Works or designee (§ 141-2).

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: Yes, for residents.

fields.label: E-waste
fields.value: May not go to the curb. It goes to the Wayne Recycling Center (§ 141-4I).

entries.title: Scavenging recyclables — Wayne Code § 141-7A
entries.name: Scavenging recyclables

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Anyone except the Township, its contractors or the owner's hauler taking or tampering with curbside recyclables, from 6:00 p.m. the day before collection for 24 hours. Once at the curb, recyclables are Township property.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $500–$1,000, with no warning required (§ 141-10B).

entries.title: Discarded refrigerators — Wayne Code § 141-6
entries.name: Discarded refrigerators

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Leaving a refrigerator, icebox or airtight container outside where children can reach it without removing the doors or latch. Doors must be off when it is set out for pickup.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: A child-entrapment hazard. Act on it immediately.

entries.title: Storm drain dumping — Wayne Code § 177-3
entries.name: Storm drain dumping

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Spilling, dumping or disposing of anything other than stormwater (oil, paint, grass, pet waste, chemicals) that sends pollutants into the Township's storm sewer system.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police Department, Director of Public Works, Township Engineer or Superintendent of Roads (§ 177-5).

fields.label: Related
fields.value: Illicit connections to the storm sewer, such as sewage or process water (§ 177-32): up to $1,000 plus cleanup after notice (§ 177-35); police enforce (§ 177-34).

entries.title: Dog running at large — Wayne Code § 68-10
entries.name: Dog running at large

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: An owner or keeper letting a dog run at large on a public street, park, public building or other public place.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: "At large" means off the owner's premises and not secured to a leash held by someone who can control it (§ 68-1).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: The ACO may impound a dog at large (§ 68-16D).

entries.title: Leash required — Wayne Code § 68-11
entries.name: Leash required

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A dog on someone else's lawn, yard, walk or driveway without permission, or on public streets or common areas of a multi-dwelling complex, unless a person has it on a leash no longer than 6 ft.

entries.title: Dog waste — Wayne Code § 68-12
entries.name: Dog waste

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A person walking a dog off their own property without a scoop and container, or failing to pick up waste right away. Covers public sidewalks, lawns, parks and buildings, private property of others, and rental property the owner leases out.

fields.label: Public education
fields.value: The handler must carry the bag and scoop, not just use one.

entries.title: Damage by dog — Wayne Code § 68-13
entries.name: Damage by dog

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Letting a dog damage another person's lawn, shrubs, flowers or property.

entries.title: Barking — Wayne Code § 68-14
entries.name: Barking

fields.value: See Noise, under Animal noise (§ 121-9G).

entries.title: Dog license, tag and rabies vaccination — Wayne Code §§ 68-2, 68-6, 68-32
entries.name: Dog license, tag and rabies vaccination

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Dogs of licensing age must be licensed each January and wear the tag on a collar or harness (§ 68-2). Licenses expire January 31 and must be renewed by February 15 (§ 68-6A). Dogs over 6 months must be rabies-vaccinated (§ 68-32A). No more than 5 dogs of licensing age at one place without a kennel license (§ 68-6C).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $10 late fee, or a summons with the § 1-15 penalty (§ 68-6.1A). Violations of the state licensing statutes are $50 per offense (§ 68-67, citing N.J.S.A. 4:19-15.19).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Animal Control Officer; Health Department.

fields.label: Related
fields.value: Removing a dog's tag or putting it on another dog is prohibited (§ 68-9).

entries.title: Interfering with animal control — Wayne Code § 68-20
entries.name: Interfering with animal control

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Hindering, molesting or interfering with an ACO or Township officer doing Chapter 68 duties.

entries.title: Cats — Wayne Code § 68-53 and § 68-55.1
entries.name: Cats

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Cats must be licensed and display the license number on a collar or by ear tattoo. An unlicensed cat may be treated as a stray (§ 68-53A). No abandoning a cat or failing to give it food, water and shelter (§ 68-55.1).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police Department and/or ACO (§ 68-56).

entries.title: Feeding waterfowl — Wayne Code § 68-44
entries.name: Feeding waterfowl

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Feeding, or allowing others to feed, waterfowl (geese, ducks, swans, gulls) anywhere in the Township.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Health Department (§ 68-43). It is also declared a public health nuisance (§ 123-3E).

entries.title: Feeding wildlife and feral cats — Wayne Code § 68-71 and § 68-77C
entries.name: Feeding wildlife and feral cats

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Feeding or baiting wildlife, including bears, deer, Canada geese, wild turkeys, pigeons and waterfowl. Feeding feral cats is prohibited unless it is part of a registered TNVM colony that meets § 68-73.

fields.label: Exempt
fields.value: Lawful hunting and fishing bait, and confined animals at zoos, petting zoos or rehabilitation centers.

fields.label: Public education
fields.value: Bird feeders that draw bears are the common complaint. This section covers "in any manner."

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 23:2A-14 (feeding black bears).

entries.title: Farm animals at large — Wayne Code § 68-42
entries.name: Farm animals at large

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Letting any farm animal run at large.

entries.title: Dogs in parks and playgrounds — Wayne Code § 129-20B(3)
entries.name: Dogs in parks and playgrounds

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Bringing a dog into a playground or onto a synthetic turf field at any time. Elsewhere in parks, dogs must be on a leash no longer than 6 ft until inside the dog park.

entries.title: Township Dog Park rules — Wayne Code § 68-68
entries.name: Township Dog Park rules

fields.label: Key rules
fields.value: Open 8 a.m. until dusk. Dogs must be registered and wear a park pass. Handlers must be 18 or older, with no more than 2 dogs each. No children under 12 inside the fence. No aggressive, sick or intact dogs. No dogs under 6 months. No prong, choke or spiked collars. No smoking, alcohol, food or glass. Handlers must clean up after their dogs.

entries.title: Dangerous and vicious dogs — Wayne Code §§ 68-59 to 68-60
entries.name: Dangerous and vicious dogs

fields.label: What it does
fields.value: Adopts the state process (N.J.S.A. 4:19-18 et seq.) in which the municipal court declares a dog potentially dangerous or vicious.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Report bites to the Health Department and ACO. The court makes the declaration on a complaint, not the officer on scene.

entries.title: Park hours and closed areas — Wayne Code § 129-20C(1) and § 129-20B(5)
entries.name: Park hours and closed areas

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Each park's open and close hours are set by Parks and Recreation and posted in the park (§ 129-20C(1)). No entering an area posted "Closed to the Public" or using an area against posted notices (§ 129-20B(5)).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Confirm the posted hours for that park. The code sets no single townwide closing time.

entries.title: Vehicles in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20A(8) and § 129-20A(9)
entries.name: Vehicles in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (8) Driving or parking off paved park roads and lots. (9) Leaving a vehicle parked in a park from a half hour after sunset until sunrise, unless permitted.

entries.title: Alcohol and drugs in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20B(1)
entries.name: Alcohol and drugs in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Bringing alcohol or a controlled dangerous substance into a park at any time, or being under their influence there.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15. See also the public open-container rule (§ 38-30A) under Alcohol.

entries.title: Smoking and vaping in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20.1
entries.name: Smoking and vaping in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Smoking, carrying anything lit, or vaping in any Township park or recreation facility, including the adjacent parking areas and driveways.

entries.title: Fireworks and fires in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20B(2) and § 129-20B(4)
entries.name: Fireworks and fires in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (2) Having, setting off or throwing fireworks or explosives in or into a park without a Parks permit. (4) Building a fire outside designated areas, or dropping lit matches or cigarettes in a park or on an abutting road.

fields.label: Related
fields.value: Leaving a picnic area before the fire is fully out (§ 129-20A(21)).

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 21:3-1 et seq. (fireworks).

entries.title: Weapons in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20A(17)
entries.name: Weapons in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Carrying or possessing firearms, air rifles, spring guns, bows and arrows, slings, blank-firing devices or traps.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: Firearm carry is governed by state law (N.J.S.A. 2C:39 and 2C:58-4.6, sensitive places). Consult the prosecutor before charging a permit holder under this local section.

entries.title: Damage, littering and wildlife in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20A(1), (4), (5), (6), (7)
entries.name: Damage, littering and wildlife in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (1) Defacing or damaging public property. (4) Cutting or damaging trees and plants, or digging up grass. (5) Hunting, trapping, harming or removing wildlife or eggs. (6) Polluting park waters, streams or storm drains. (7) Dumping or leaving trash outside receptacles; carry it out if there are none.

entries.title: Water, ice and boats in parks — Wayne Code § 129-20A(12), (14), (16) and § 129-20B(7)
entries.name: Water, ice and boats in parks

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Swimming or wading outside designated areas (A(12)). Boats or rafts outside designated boating areas (A(14)). Fishing where bathing is allowed (A(16)). Going onto the ice except in a designated skating area with the safety signal displayed (B(7)).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: The ice rule is a life-safety rule. Order people off immediately.

entries.title: Other park conduct — Wayne Code § 129-20A and § 129-20B
entries.name: Other park conduct

fields.label: A(22)
fields.value: No overnight camping, tents or shelters, and no trailers or campers left after closing, without a permit.

fields.label: A(23)
fields.value: Ball games and thrown objects only in designated areas. Skateboarding and roller-skating only in areas built for them.

fields.label: A(24)
fields.value: No horseback riding in any public park or public place.

fields.label: A(10)–(11)
fields.value: Ride bicycles safely, and don't leave a bike where people can trip on it.

fields.label: B(6)
fields.value: No gambling except where designated.

fields.label: B(8)
fields.value: Produce a park permit on request.

fields.label: B(9)
fields.value: Don't interfere with a group using an area under permit.

fields.label: B(10)
fields.value: No selling or vendor carts without a Parks concession.

fields.label: B(11)
fields.value: No posting signs or flyers on parkland.

entries.title: Smoking on Township property — Wayne Code § 90-35
entries.name: Smoking on Township property

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Smoking, carrying anything lit, or vaping anywhere on municipally owned property, including offices, sidewalks, grass, parking lots and drive aisles.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15, with a $250 minimum for a first violation (§ 90-36).

entries.title: Library property — Wayne Code §§ 109-2, 109-3, 109-5
entries.name: Library property

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Willfully destroying library materials (§ 109-2). Borrowing with a false name or someone else's card with intent to defraud (§ 109-3). Removing materials without following borrowing rules (§ 109-5).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Chapter 109 lists none of its own; § 1-15 applies by default.

entries.title: Open container and drinking in public — Wayne Code § 38-30A
entries.name: Open container and drinking in public

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Drinking alcohol, or having an opened container with alcohol still in it, in a public area without a permit.

fields.label: "Public area" (§ 38-29)
fields.value: Parks, playgrounds, trails and recreation areas; streets, sidewalks, parking lots and garages, walkways and rest areas, including the semipublic lots in § 200-35; scenic and historic sites; school and public building sites; and the inside of a private vehicle on a public street, lane, lot or other public or quasi-public place.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police.

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: No.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: A permit needs Township Clerk approval and NJ ABC approval. Ask to see it at events.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 39:4-51b (open container in a motor vehicle).

entries.title: Discarding alcohol containers — Wayne Code § 38-30B
entries.name: Discarding alcohol containers

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Throwing an alcohol container on a street, sidewalk, public lot, public or quasi-public place, or someone else's private property without consent.

entries.title: Underage possession or drinking on private property — Wayne Code § 38-33
entries.name: Underage possession or drinking on private property

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A person under the legal age knowingly possessing or consuming alcohol on private property without legal authority.

fields.label: Exceptions
fields.value: A religious observance; or in the presence of, and with permission of, a parent, guardian or relative of legal age. Also exempt are underage employees of a Title 33 licensee and culinary or hotel management students preparing food.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $250 for a first offense and $350 after that. The court may also suspend or postpone driving privileges for 6 months (§ 38-34).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: (1) The 911 medical amnesty in N.J.S.A. 40:48-1.2a gives immunity to the underage caller, up to two people with them, and the person who needed help, if they meet the statute's conditions. (2) NJ's 2021 cannabis and underage-possession reforms changed how juveniles are handled. Confirm current procedure with the prosecutor before charging anyone under 18.

entries.title: Bar and liquor store hours — Wayne Code § 38-16
entries.name: Bar and liquor store hours

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A licensee selling, serving or delivering alcohol, allowing drinking, or allowing anyone except listed cleanup employees on the premises: 3:00–6:00 a.m. on weekdays and Saturdays; 3:00–10:00 a.m. on Sundays; 5:00–10:00 a.m. on New Year's Day.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: Only employees listed on the ABC E-141-A form may stay to clean up. Restaurants, motels and bowling alleys may stay open for their other business only (§ 38-16B).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: License suspension or revocation through ABC/Council (§ 38-28).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Document the time, the people present and any service, and forward it to ABC and the Clerk.

entries.title: Licensee serving under-21s — Wayne Code § 38-17
entries.name: Licensee serving under-21s

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: A licensee selling or serving alcohol to anyone under 21, or allowing them to drink on the premises.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 38-28 (license action).

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 33:1-77 (sale to minors) and N.J.S.A. 33:1-81 (minor entering to purchase, or false age). § 38-18 requires the "Minors Take Notice" sign.

entries.title: Tobacco and vape sales to under-21s — Wayne Code § 90-32
entries.name: Tobacco and vape sales to under-21s

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Selling tobacco or nicotine delivery products to anyone under 21 (§ 90-32B). Self-service displays and vending machines are banned (§ 90-32A). Clerks must check government photo ID for anyone 26 or younger and post proof-of-age signs at least 6 in. x 8 in. (§ 90-32C–D).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15, with a $250 minimum for a first violation (§ 90-36). Each sale is a separate violation (§ 90-34A).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Health Officer or designee. Police assist on request (§ 90-33).

entries.title: Smoking in hotel and motel rooms — Wayne Code § 94-21
entries.name: Smoking in hotel and motel rooms

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Smoking in any guest room of a hotel, motel or other lodging in the Township.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Fines under N.J.S.A. 26:3D-62 (§ 94-22).
Smoking in parks (§ 129-20.1) and on Township property (§ 90-35) is under Parks and Public Property.

entries.title: Off-road and low-speed vehicles — Wayne Code § 202-5A
entries.name: Off-road and low-speed vehicles

fields.value: No operation between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.
A factory or equivalent muffler is required.
Not within 400 ft of an affected person's occupied property. No violation exists if the NCO or NCI finds the use is not affecting the complainant.
Not on another person's private property without the owner's or occupant's prior express permission.
Not on public grounds without permission.
No loud, unnecessary or unusual noise that disturbs others.
No careless, reckless or negligent operation.
Not on any public street in Wayne.
Not on Township athletic fields, courts, grass areas or natural-surface trails.

fields.label: Exceptions (§ 202-4)
fields.value: Farming, yard work and snow removal; Township and emergency use; travel to and from a road or loading for transport; mowers and lawn equipment; Township-permitted events; permitted racetracks; MSF-type safety training with Township permission; and maintenance runs 8 a.m.–8 p.m. of no more than 15 minutes an hour, twice a day.

entries.title: E-bikes, e-scooters and motorized bicycles — Wayne Code § 202-5B
entries.name: E-bikes, e-scooters and motorized bicycles

fields.value: No careless, reckless or negligent operation, including failing to yield to pedestrians.
Must obey traffic signals, signs and control devices, unless directed by an officer.
Not on Township athletic fields, courts, grass areas or natural-surface trails.
E-bikes may not be ridden on a road with a speed limit over 25 mph.
No passengers.
E-bike riders under 17 must wear a helmet.
No parking an e-bike or e-scooter so that it blocks a sidewalk.
Motorized bicycle operators must be at least 15, licensed, registered and insured. Every motorized bicycle rider must wear a helmet, whatever their age.
No handheld phone or electronic device while riding. Hands-free use is allowed.
Front and rear reflectors are required. At night, a white front lamp and a red rear lamp, each visible at 500 ft.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Classify the device first using the table above, since the rules differ by type. A "motorized bicycle" needs a license, registration and insurance; a Class 1 or 2 e-bike does not.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.16 (low-speed e-bikes and e-scooters), N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3 et seq. (motorized bicycles), N.J.S.A. 39:4-10.1 (helmets).

entries.title: Motor vehicles on school paths — Wayne Code § 180-34
entries.name: Motor vehicles on school paths

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Driving any type of motor vehicle on a school path, whether on public or private property.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Article VII sets none of its own; § 1-15 applies by default.

entries.title: Sidewalk snow and ice (homes and businesses) — Wayne Code § 180-20
entries.name: Sidewalk snow and ice (homes and businesses)

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: The owner or tenant of land abutting a public-street sidewalk must clear snow and ice within 48 hours after the snow falls or the ice forms, leaving a clear path at least 36 inches wide.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $100 per violation (§ 180-25). The Township may clear it and lien the cost (§§ 180-23, 180-24).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: The Township Engineer, Director of Public Works or any police officer may issue a notice of violation or a summons (§ 180-23A).

fields.label: Warning first
fields.value: Not required. The Township clears after the 48 hours pass.

entries.title: Plowing or blowing snow into the street — Wayne Code § 180-22
entries.name: Plowing or blowing snow into the street

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Placing, throwing or depositing snow, ice, brush or vegetation onto the roadway between the curblines of a public street.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $100 per violation for purposefully depositing snow on the roadway (§ 180-25).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Engineer, Director of Public Works or any police officer (§ 180-23A).

fields.label: Public education
fields.value: This covers plow contractors and landscapers too, not just homeowners.

entries.title: Snow at apartments, condos and shopping centers — Wayne Code §§ 169-1, 169-2, 169-4
entries.name: Snow at apartments, condos and shopping centers

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: Owners of multi-dwelling developments with 3 or more units (§ 169-1) and of shopping centers or commercial properties (§ 169-2) must clear private streets, walkways, lots open to the public and the area around dumpsters within 12 hours after the storm ends. Walks must be cleared at least 36 in. wide (§ 169-4).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15 (§ 169-5). After a notice of violation expires, the Township clears it, issues a summons and liens the cost (§ 169-6).

entries.title: Unaccepted development streets — Wayne Code § 180-35
entries.name: Unaccepted development streets

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: The developer must clear unaccepted dedicated streets within 6 hours after the snowfall ends, to at least 25 ft wide. If accumulation passes 6 in., plowing must continue during the storm.

entries.title: Sidewalk vegetation — Wayne Code § 180-21
entries.name: Sidewalk vegetation

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: Owners or tenants must keep the sidewalk area clear of vegetation that obstructs pedestrians, or at least 8 ft high where there is no sidewalk. They must clear it within 3 days after notice.

entries.title: Objects and obstructions in the street or right-of-way — Wayne Code § 180-10
entries.name: Objects and obstructions in the street or right-of-way

fields.label: § 180-10I
fields.value: No permanent or temporary object or structure in the roadway or right-of-way (portable basketball hoops, rocks, posts) without Council approval. Compliant mailboxes, and refuse and cans on collection days, are allowed.

fields.label: § 180-10G
fields.value: No brush, hedges or objects over 2½ ft high within 10 ft of a roadway and 25 ft of an intersection if they block drivers' view.

fields.label: § 180-10H
fields.value: No vegetation over the roadway lower than 17 ft.

fields.label: § 180-10F
fields.value: No storing building materials, dirt, equipment or sheds on a street, except during road or utility work.

fields.label: § 180-10C–D
fields.value: No obstructing street drainage, or pumping sumps into the gutter in a way that creates an icing hazard.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: The Township Engineer issues a 10-day written order to comply (§ 180-11A). Patrol should report the condition.

entries.title: High grass, weeds and property upkeep — Wayne Code § 99-1 (International Property Maintenance Code)
entries.name: High grass, weeds and property upkeep

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Wayne adopts the 2015 IPMC with local amendments. Grass and weeds may be no taller than 8 inches (IPMC § 302.4 as amended by § 99-1B(11)). Fences, sheds, signs and walls must be kept sound (IPMC § 302.7, § 99-1B(12)).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Construction Official or designee (§ 99-1C). Refer it.

entries.title: Graffiti — Wayne Code § 197-2 and § 197-3
entries.name: Graffiti

fields.value: The owner must remove graffiti within 30 days after a written notice from the Code Enforcement Official. The Township may then remove it and lien the cost.
Anyone under 18 may not possess a graffiti implement (spray paint, indelible marker) for the purpose of criminal mischief.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.S.A. 2C:17-3 (criminal mischief and graffiti).

entries.title: House numbers — Wayne Code § 57-4
entries.name: House numbers

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: Arabic numerals at least 3 in. high (5 in. if the building is more than 50 ft from the street), readable from the street centerline and visible at night by spotlight. If not visible on the building, they go on a post or fence within 15 ft of the curb.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15, after one month's written notice (§ 57-7).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Construction Official (§ 57-6).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Report addresses you couldn't find on a call so they can be referred.

entries.title: Storage containers (PODs) at homes — Wayne Code § 176-4
entries.name: Storage containers (PODs) at homes

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Allowed only with an active construction permit and Construction Official approval. One container only, no larger than 20 ft x 8 ft, not on wheels, and at least 10 ft from any property line unless fully in a paved driveway. Non-construction storage falls under § 134-67.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Construction Official (§ 176-7).

entries.title: Problem rentals: landlord bond — Wayne Code § 99-19
entries.name: Problem rentals: landlord bond

fields.label: What it does
fields.value: A landlord of a building with no more than 4 units can be required to post a $500–$5,000 bond after two convictions of tenants within 24 months for Title 2C or municipal disorderly-conduct offenses at or near the rental.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Sign complaints against tenants at disorderly rentals and document the address. Convictions feed this process (§ 99-18).

entries.title: False burglar, panic and medical alarms — Wayne Code § 36-3 and § 36-5
entries.name: False burglar, panic and medical alarms

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: (A) Causing or allowing a false alarm signal from any location. (B) Causing a report that brings a police, fire or medical response and turns out to be unfounded.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Wayne Police Department (§ 36-2). Every false alarm is investigated and recorded (§ 36-4A).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: An alarm the central station cancels before police or EMS arrive does not count. Fire alarms cannot be canceled (§ 36-5C).

header: False alarms in a calendar year

fields.value: The code's tables skip the 7th alarm; it goes from the 6th to "in excess of 7." Confirm with the prosecutor how a 7th alarm is charged.

entries.title: Outdoor alarm sounding over 15 minutes — Wayne Code § 36-4B
entries.name: Outdoor alarm sounding over 15 minutes

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: An exterior or outdoor audible alarm that keeps sounding more than 15 minutes after activation.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $100–$1,250 on conviction.

fields.label: Related
fields.value: The responsible person must designate a keyholder with authority to disable the alarm and give that contact to the central station (§ 36-4C). Also see § 121-9E under Noise.

entries.title: False fire alarms — Wayne Code § 14-9 and § 14-9.1
entries.name: False fire alarms

fields.label: What it covers
fields.value: Fire, smoke, sprinkler water-flow and CO alarms not caused by fire, smoke or a condition beyond the owner's control. Police report every false fire alarm to the Fire Bureau, which investigates and keeps the count (§ 14-9B).

fields.label: Penalty (§ 14-9.1)
fields.value: Multifamily complexes, businesses and commercial: first 2 warnings, then $200, $300, $500, and $1,000 for the 6th and beyond. Single-family homes, townhouses and condo units: first 2 warnings, then $100, $200, $300, and $500 for the 6th and beyond. Contractors or workers who trigger one: $200–$1,000 each (§ 14-9.1C).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Fire Bureau.

entries.title: Tampering with or blocking fire systems — Wayne Code § 14-10
entries.name: Tampering with or blocking fire systems

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Blocking access to, interfering or tampering with, or damaging any fire alarm, suppression, detection or firefighting system or device.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Mandatory $500 per day per violation, including during an actual alarm. A summons issues if it is not corrected.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Fire Bureau.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: N.J.A.C. 5:70 (NJ Uniform Fire Code), which the Fire Bureau enforces locally (§ 14-1).

entries.title: Obstructing hydrant access — Wayne Code § 14-15
entries.name: Obstructing hydrant access

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Bumps, fences, gates, bars, pipes, horses or any other obstruction that blocks access to a hydrant on any street, including private streets and access lanes.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Up to $500 per day (§ 14-15D).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Fire Official (§ 14-15E).

fields.label: Related
fields.value: Vehicles parked within 10 ft of a hydrant: § 205-38B (see Parking).

entries.title: Unauthorized hydrant use — Wayne Code § 14-12
entries.name: Unauthorized hydrant use

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Opening or using a fire hydrant without permission from the Fire Official and the Supervisor of Water and Sewers.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Up to $500 per violation.

entries.title: Pyrotechnics indoors at businesses — Wayne Code § 14-23
entries.name: Pyrotechnics indoors at businesses

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Lighting, displaying, possessing or using pyrotechnics, sparklers or smoke or fog machines inside any commercial structure.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $1,000 per occurrence.

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: This is common at restaurant birthday celebrations (sparklers on bottles or cakes) and banquet halls.

entries.title: Open burning — Wayne Code § 123-3H
entries.name: Open burning

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Open burning of refuse or plant life (leaf or brush piles) or salvage operations, unless allowed under Chapter 32.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Health Officer or designee (§ 123-5). Chapter 32 adopts the state air pollution code, enforced by the Passaic County Department of Health (§ 32-1B).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Handle the fire hazard first, then refer to Health.

entries.title: Garage sales and flea markets — Wayne Code §§ 151-2, 151-3, 151-4
entries.name: Garage sales and flea markets

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: A permit from the Construction Official is required and must be displayed at the sale (§ 151-2A). Each sale may run up to 2 consecutive weekends, with no more than 2 permits per owner per year. Hours are 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. only (§ 151-3). Signs must be removed within 24 hours after the sale and may not go on utility poles, light standards, the right-of-way or trees (§ 151-4B–C).

fields.label: Exempt
fields.value: The town-wide garage sale on the last two weekends of April needs no permit, but the other rules apply (§ 151-2B).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Construction Code Official (§ 151-5). Refer it.

entries.title: Temporary signs on residential property — Wayne Code § 134-68.1I(2)
entries.name: Temporary signs on residential property

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: No permit is needed for event, sale, construction, political or advocacy signs, but each must show the name of the person or group responsible. Signs may not be lit or attached to utility poles, light stands or trees. They are limited to 12 sq ft total per property, may go in front or side yards, and never in the public right-of-way. Signs in the right-of-way may be removed by the Township.

fields.label: Political and noncommercial signs (§ 59-2)
fields.value: The candidate or group files an information sheet with the Clerk before putting signs up. The designated person must remove an improper sign within 24 hours of notice.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Zoning Officer.

fields.label: Commercial temporary signs (§ 134-68.1I(1))
fields.value: A zoning permit is required. They may stay up no more than 30 days, are limited to 15 sq ft (banners 32 sq ft), and may not go in the right-of-way.

entries.title: Food trucks and ice cream trucks — Wayne Code §§ 149-5, 149-12, 149-15
entries.name: Food trucks and ice cream trucks

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: The vendor must hold a Health Officer license and post a price sign on the vehicle (§ 149-5). The license certificate must be displayed where patrons can see it (§ 149-12). An itinerant vendor may stay in one area no more than 30 minutes a day (§ 149-4).

fields.label: Prohibits (§ 149-15)
fields.value: Stopping to sell in a public or quasi-public place on any municipal, county or state road or right-of-way, or within 1,000 ft of the front door of a Township-licensed food business. Construction sites are exempt from the 1,000-ft rule.

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15 (§ 149-18). The Health Officer may also suspend the license (§ 149-16).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Health Officer licenses vendors. The code doesn't name police for this article, so document and refer.

entries.title: Landscapers — Wayne Code § 106-4
entries.name: Landscapers

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: (A) Company name, address and phone on both sides of every vehicle. (B) A Township decal on the front bumper and trailer, unless the company is registered under the state Home Improvement Contractor Act. (C) Three cones at least 18 in. tall behind each parked vehicle. (D) Tarps over yard waste in transit, and the company cleans up any spill. (E) No blowing grass or yard waste into the street and leaving it there.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Wayne Police Department or the Health Officer (§ 106-7).

entries.title: Secondhand gold and jewelry dealers — Wayne Code §§ 154-5, 154-6, 154-7
entries.name: Secondhand gold and jewelry dealers

fields.label: Requires
fields.value: Dealers must send the Chief a description and photos of every item bought, received or sold within 48 hours (§ 154-5). Items must be held for 45 days without selling or melting them and made available to police on request (§ 154-6). Dealers must ID every seller and may not deal with minors or anyone intoxicated or impaired (§ 154-7).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15 (§ 154-9). The Chief may revoke the license after a hearing (§ 154-8).

entries.title: Towing (police rotation) — Wayne Code § 191-7
entries.name: Towing (police rotation)

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: Only Wayne PD may call out towers and change the rotation (§ 191-7B, 7D). Towers may not cruise for business (§ 191-7E). Licensed towers must show they can guarantee a 15-minute response time (§ 191-3).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $100–$500 for a first offense; $500–$1,000 for a second within a year; at least $1,000 and a one-year license suspension for a third within a year (§ 191-16).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Chief of Police (§ 191-15C).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: Chapter 191 does not cover tows from private property. Those fall under state rule N.J.A.C. 13:45A-31.6 (§ 191-1C).

entries.title: Shopping carts — Wayne Code §§ 162-2, 162-3, 112-13
entries.name: Shopping carts

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Taking a cart off store premises beyond the pickup area (§ 162-2), or abandoning a cart on a sidewalk, street or other property (§ 162-3). The store must mark carts with its name and "removal prohibited" and keep its lot clear (§ 112-13).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: $100–$1,000 (§ 162-7). The store is held responsible and has 10 days after notice to fix the problem before a summons (§ 162-5).

entries.title: Urinating or defecating in public — Wayne Code § 123-4.2
entries.name: Urinating or defecating in public

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Urinating or defecating on any street, sidewalk or other public or semi-public place, or anywhere in public view, except in a restroom. Also prohibited on private property outdoors without the owner's or occupant's consent.

fields.label: Elements
fields.value: "Public view" means somewhere the act may reasonably be expected to be seen by others.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Chief of Police or designee (§ 123-5).

entries.title: Discharging firearms and weapons — Wayne Code § 77-3
entries.name: Discharging firearms and weapons

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Carrying or discharging any firearm, bow and arrow, crossbow, air-driven weapon (BB or pellet gun), slingshot or other weapon in the Township, except as § 77-4 allows.

fields.label: Exceptions (§ 77-4)
fields.value: Supervised ranges; law enforcement and Fish and Wildlife on duty; defense of self, family, guests or property; ceremonial salutes (not holiday celebration shooting); state depredation permit holders; and unloaded transport under N.J.S.A. 2C:39-6.

fields.label: State overlap — verify
fields.value: Firearm carry is governed by state law (N.J.S.A. 2C:39-5 and 2C:58-4). Use § 77-3 for discharge complaints, such as backyard BB guns or archery, and confirm with the prosecutor before charging any carry offense under this local section.

entries.title: Short-term rentals (29 days or less) — Wayne Code § 94-23 and § 94-24
entries.name: Short-term rentals (29 days or less)

fields.label: Prohibits
fields.value: Renting a dwelling or its land for payment for 29 days or less (§ 94-23A), and advertising such a rental (§ 94-24). Adopted 3-4-2026.

fields.label: Exempt
fields.value: Licensed hotels and motels; state-protected group homes; rentals of 30 days or more; and guests who pay nothing (§ 94-23B).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: Civil penalty under § 1-15, regardless of intent or knowledge. It is also declared a nuisance per se (§ 94-25B–C).

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Police Department, Building Code Official, Fire Official, Health Department and others (§ 94-25A).

fields.label: Officer tip
fields.value: At party or disturbance calls, ask whether the occupants are short-term renters and document the platform listing.

entries.title: Lawn watering days — Wayne Code § 205-34
entries.name: Lawn watering days

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: On Township water, even-numbered addresses may water lawns and landscaping Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Odd-numbered addresses may water Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. On Sundays, only plants and shrubs may be watered, at any address.

fields.label: Exempt
fields.value: New plantings for 30 days, farms, nurseries and athletic fields. Car washing, power washing, fountains and pool filling are not covered.

fields.label: Enforced by
fields.value: Division of Water and Sewers.

entries.title: Boats on Township waters — Wayne Code §§ 53-1 to 53-7
entries.name: Boats on Township waters

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: A muffler is required (§ 53-1). Motors may be no more than 10 hp, inboard or outboard, except police and municipal boats (§§ 53-2, 53-3). No loud noise, profanity, shouting or disturbing the peace from a boat (§ 53-4). Speed limit 10 mph (§ 53-5). Motorboats may run from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset on weekdays, and from 12:00 noon to one hour after sunset on Sundays (§ 53-6). No motors in the listed Ramapo River areas, no boating on floodwaters outside normal channels except for emergencies or access to one's own property, and no wakes that wash floodwater against buildings (§ 53-7).

entries.title: Swimming facilities — Wayne Code § 129-3 and § 129-3.1
entries.name: Swimming facilities

fields.label: Rules
fields.value: No entering or using Township swim facilities outside posted days and hours (§ 129-3). No swimming without a lifeguard on duty (§ 129-3.1).

fields.label: Penalty
fields.value: § 1-15 (§ 129-7A). Members who strike or threaten staff are removed immediately, their membership is revoked, and police are notified (§ 129-2.1D).

notVerified.label: Searched for, not in the Wayne code.
notVerified.value: Use state law or another section instead.

notVerified.label: Fireworks (general)
notVerified.value: No townwide fireworks ordinance. Wayne regulates fireworks only in parks (§ 129-20B(2)) and indoors at businesses (§ 14-23). Use N.J.S.A. 21:3-1 et seq.

notVerified.label: Fire lanes
notVerified.value: No standalone fire-lane ordinance. Fire zones on private lots are enforceable only where that property's § 200-35 schedule covers them. Otherwise use N.J.S.A. 39:4-138 or refer to the Fire Bureau (Uniform Fire Code).

notVerified.label: Skateboards and scooters in the street
notVerified.value: The only rule is in parks (§ 129-20A(23)). E-scooters are covered under § 202-5B.

notVerified.label: Public cannabis use
notVerified.value: No municipal ordinance found. Use state law.

notVerified.label: Residential RV and trailer parking on the street
notVerified.value: No street-specific RV ban found beyond the 2–6 a.m. overnight rule (§ 200-5B). Driveway rules are in § 134-67.1.
Flyers: § 112-4F says up to $100, while § 112-16C says up to $500.
